title: Locally finite type monomorphisms between qcqs spaces are quasi-affine
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. A morphism is quasi-affine if it is representable by schemes and every pullback along an affine scheme test is a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Let $A$ and $B$ be quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces and let $u:A\to B$ be locally of finite type. If $u$ is a monomorphism, meaning that $A(T)\to B(T)$ is injective for every $S$-scheme $T$, then $u$ is quasi-affine.

proof.text: The assumed quasi-compact etale atlas of $A$ makes $|A|$ quasi-compact by the last sentence of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. The same last sentence, applied to an assumed quasi-compact atlas of each affine-test pullback of the absolute diagonal $B\to B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}B$, shows that these pullbacks have quasi-compact point spaces, so $B$ is quasi-separated in the point-space sense of [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. Since $|A|$ is quasi-compact and $B$ is quasi-separated in that sense, [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] implies that $u$ is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests in the point-space sense. For each such test, [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] converts the quasi-compact point space of the pullback into an affine surjective etale atlas. Thus the atlas and point-space conventions agree for these pullbacks. Together with the assumed local finite type, this says that $u$ is of finite type in the algebraic-space convention of [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], which explicitly agrees with the ordinary algebraic-space notion. The quasi-separatedness of $A$ and quasi-compactness of $B$ are allowed but not needed here.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$ and a map $h_T\to B$, form $E=A\times_Bh_T$ using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The map $v:E\to h_T$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], which gives arbitrary base-change stability and agreement with the algebraic-space notions. It is a monomorphism directly: a section over $H$ is a pair $(a,t)$ with $u(a)$ equal to the image of $t$; two such pairs with the same $t$ have the same $a$ by the injectivity of $A(H)\to B(H)$. Thus $v$ is locally of finite type and a monomorphism, with a scheme target.

source.place: Tag 0463 (lemma-monomorphism-loc-finite-type-loc-quasi-finite), reduction to scheme tests; Tag 03XH (lemma-base-change-finite-type); stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06FU (lemma-base-change-finite-type).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-lft-monomorphism-separated-lqf] to $v:E\to h_T$. Its hypotheses are exactly the monomorphism and chartwise local finite type proved in step 2. It gives a diagonal which is a closed immersion on every scheme base change and chartwise local quasi-finiteness. These are precisely the two hypotheses of [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable], so there is a $T$-scheme $Z_T$ with $h_{Z_T}\simeq E$ over $h_T$. Since $T\to B$ was arbitrary, this proves representability of $u$ by schemes, not just representability over etale charts.

Now let $T$ be affine. Write $v_T:Z_T\to T$ for the represented map. Its local finite type and local quasi-finiteness follow from the chart tests of steps 2-3 by taking the identity chart of $Z_T$; its separatedness is the diagonal assertion of step 3 on scheme tests. Its source is quasi-compact since $u$ is quasi-compact and $T$ is an affine test (step 1); equivalently $v_T$ is quasi-compact, also part of its finite-type assertion in step 2. Therefore [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism-of-quasi-finite] applies to $v_T$, with all four hypotheses: separated, quasi-compact, locally quasi-finite and locally of finite type. It is a quasi-affine scheme morphism. By [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], taking the affine open $T$ itself, $Z_T$ is a quasi-affine scheme: a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Together with representability from step 3, this is exactly the asserted quasi-affineness of $u$.
